text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy..

- The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) wants stiffer penalties against employers who fail to deposit their mandatory contributions despite repeated reminders. The EPF filed suits against a total of 2,108 employers this year against 2,057 last year.

- All 46 foreigners who were in Kuala Lumpur to attend the Second East Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor were deported and 40 Malaysian NGO activists were freed by Monday. The National Union of Journalists called the detention of journalists in the break up of the conference a blow to press freedom.

- Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) and its subsidiary Cellular Communications Network (M) Sdn Bhd denied they were facing any management problems over servicing their loans. The statement from the companies was in response to a news story that the company was facing a cash flow problem.

- Four business deals signed between Ghana and Malaysia during Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's visit were expected to further boost ties between the two countries. The deals were for the development of an export processing zone, highway construction and mineral exploration in Ghana.

- Malaysia's second geosynchronous communications satellite, Measat 2, will be launched from Kourou in French Guiana on Wednesday. The launch will be witnessed by Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
- Malaysia's light rail transit (LRT) in Kuala Lumpur will start its services next month. The LRT system is widely expected to ease the growing traffic congestion in Kuala Lumpur and its suburbs.
- Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd-Diperdana Corp Bhd group has bought a large stake in Sabah-based shipping company Chong Fui Shipping Sdn Bhd, sources said.

- Commerce MGI Sdn Bhd is expected to issue U.S. dollar denominated islamic securities by early next year. The securities issue will be worth about $300 million, CMGI's chief executive Hasnita Hashim told Star Business.
